replies.text:
I'll review EVAL-07 and build the threat model, then submit it.

Looking at the context:
- **Issue**: Logging request bodies in an API gateway
- **Design**: The API gateway logs full request and response bodies, including login requests and payment details, to the central log system for 1 year
- **Data classes**: credentials, payment
- **Exposure**: internal

This design has critical security flaws around logging sensitive data. Let me build the threat model:

```json
{
  "schema": "redline.threatmodel.v1",
  "issueKey": "EVAL-07",
  "sketch": {
    "components": ["API gateway", "Central log system", "Log storage", "Login endpoint", "Payment endpoint"],
    "dataStores": ["Log storage"],
    "externalServices": [],
    "trustBoundaries": ["Between API gateway and operators", "Between log system and personnel"],
    "dataClasses": ["credentials", "payment"],
    "exposure": "internal",
    "llmFeatures": false
  },
  "threats": [
    {
      "stride": "InformationDisclosure",
      "title": "Passwords logged in plaintext in login requests",
      "scenario": "The API gateway logs request bodies for login endpoints, including user passwords. Anyone with access to the central log system—developers, operators, support staff, or an attacker who compromises log access—can retrieve these passwords and use them to take over user accounts.",
      "component": "API gateway",
      "likelihood": 5,
      "impact": 5,
      "evidence": [
        {
          "quote": "logs full request and response bodies, including login requests"
        }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V7.1.1", "V9.2.1"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-532", "CWE-312"],
      "plainLanguage": "User passwords are being saved in logs where anyone with system access can read them and log in as those users",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Login credentials must be excluded from logs",
        "given": "a user submits a login request with their password",
        "when": "the API gateway logs the request",
        "then": "the password field is redacted or the request body is not logged"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "InformationDisclosure",
      "title": "Payment card data logged in plaintext",
      "scenario": "Full payment request bodies containing credit card numbers, CVV codes, and cardholder data are logged. This violates PCI-DSS requirements. If an attacker gains access to logs, or if logs are accidentally exposed, customers are at risk of payment fraud.",
      "component": "API gateway",
      "likelihood": 5,
      "impact": 5,
      "evidence": [
        {
          "quote": "including login requests and payment details"
        }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V7.1.1", "V8.3.4"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-532", "CWE-359"],
      "plainLanguage": "Credit card numbers and security codes are being saved in logs, which breaks payment card industry rules and puts customers at risk",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Payment card data must be excluded from logs",
        "given": "a user submits payment information",
        "when": "the API gateway logs the request",
        "then": "card numbers, CVVs, and other cardholder data are redacted or the request body is not logged"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "Spoofing",
      "title": "Session tokens logged in responses enabling session hijacking",
      "scenario": "Login and authentication responses contain session tokens that the API gateway logs. An attacker with log access can extract valid session tokens and use them to impersonate users without needing their passwords.",
      "component": "API gateway",
      "likelihood": 5,
      "impact": 4,
      "evidence": [
        {
          "quote": "logs full request and response bodies"
        }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V7.1.1", "V3.2.1"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-532"],
      "plainLanguage": "Login session tokens are saved in logs, letting someone copy them and pretend to be another user",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Session tokens must be excluded from logs",
        "given": "a response contains a session token",
        "when": "the API gateway logs the response",
        "then": "session tokens are redacted"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "InformationDisclosure",
      "title": "One-year log retention extends window for credential and payment data exposure",
      "scenario": "Credentials and payment data remain accessible in logs for a full year. If the log system is compromised at any point during that period, attackers gain access to a year's worth of sensitive data, vastly increasing the scale and impact of the breach.",
      "component": "Log storage",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "evidence": [
        {
          "quote": "to the central log system for 1 year"
        }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V8.3.5"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-312"],
      "plainLanguage": "Keeping passwords and payment details in logs for a full year means more time for them to be stolen",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Logs containing sensitive data must have minimal retention",
        "given": "logs contain request or response bodies",
        "when": "retention policies are applied",
        "then": "logs are deleted after the minimum time needed for debugging, not one year"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "InformationDisclosure",
      "title": "Excessive access to central log system exposes sensitive data",
      "scenario": "Multiple teams (development, operations, support) have access to the central log system for debugging. With credentials and payment data in logs, any team member can intentionally or accidentally access sensitive data they should not see, increasing insider threat risk.",
      "component": "Central log system",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "evidence": [
        {
          "quote": "to the central log system"
        }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V7.1.3"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-532"],
      "plainLanguage": "Too many people can access logs that contain passwords and payment info",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Access to logs with sensitive data must be strictly controlled",
        "given": "logs may contain sensitive data",
        "when": "users request log access",
        "then": "access is granted only to minimal personnel, requires justification, and is audited"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "InformationDisclosure",
      "title": "Compromise of log system exposes year's worth of credentials and payment data",
      "scenario": "An attacker exploits a vulnerability in the central log system or compromises an account with log access. They gain access to a year of plaintext passwords and payment card data for all users, enabling mass account takeover and payment fraud.",
      "component": "Central log system",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 5,
      "evidence": [
        {
          "quote": "to the central log system for 1 year"
        }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V9.1.1"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-532", "CWE-312"],
      "plainLanguage": "If someone hacks into the log system, they get everyone's passwords and credit cards for the entire year",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Central log system must be hardened against compromise",
        "given": "logs are stored in a centralized system",
        "when": "the system is deployed",
        "then": "logs are encrypted at rest, the system is network-isolated, access is monitored, and intrusion detection is active"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

Submitting this threat model now...
